places.title: Great Pyramid of Giza
places.note:
Built for the pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC. The oldest of the seven, and the only one still standing.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza

places.title: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
places.note:
Terraced gardens said to have been built in Babylon, perhaps by Nebuchadnezzar II. No trace has been found, and some historians doubt they existed.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging_Gardens_of_Babylon

places.title: Temple of Artemis
places.note:
A huge Greek temple at Ephesus, rebuilt after it was burned down in 356 BC. A single re-erected column marks the site today.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_of_Artemis

places.title: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
places.note:
A seated ivory-and-gold statue about 12 m tall, made by the sculptor Phidias around 435 BC. Lost in antiquity.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Zeus_at_Olympia

places.title: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
places.note:
The tomb of Mausolus, which gave us the word “mausoleum”. Ruined by earthquakes; its stones were reused in Bodrum Castle.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausoleum_at_Halicarnassus

places.title: Colossus of Rhodes
places.note:
A bronze statue of the sun god Helios, about 33 m tall. It stood for only 54 years before an earthquake toppled it in 226 BC.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colossus_of_Rhodes

places.title: Lighthouse of Alexandria
places.note:
Built on the island of Pharos around 280 BC. Wrecked by earthquakes; the Citadel of Qaitbay now stands on its site.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_of_Alexandria

places.title: Google
places.note:
The Googleplex, Google's headquarters.
https://www.google.com/about/careers/

places.title: NVIDIA
places.note:
NVIDIA's headquarters, a short drive from the Googleplex.
https://www.nvidia.com

places.title: Keen Technologies
places.note:
John Carmack's AGI company. The pin marks Dallas, not a specific office.
https://keenagi.com

places.title: Black Forest Labs
places.note:
Makers of the FLUX image models. The pin marks Freiburg, not a specific office.
https://bfl.ai

places.title: TSMC
places.note:
The world's largest contract chipmaker. Headquarters and Fab 12A.
https://www.tsmc.com

places.title: ASUS
places.note:
ASUS headquarters in Beitou, northern Taipei.
https://www.asus.com

places.title: Sakana AI
places.note:
AI research lab founded in 2023 by former Google researchers. The pin marks central Tokyo, not a specific office.
https://sakana.ai

places.title: Nintendo
places.note:
Nintendo's headquarters in southern Kyoto.
https://www.nintendo.co.jp

places.title: Pioneer Center for AI
places.note:
Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence: interdisciplinary, fundamental AI research, co-financed by the Danish ministry, the universities and five private foundations.
https://www.aicentre.dk

places.title: Plitvice Lakes
places.note:
Sixteen terraced lakes joined by waterfalls, in Croatia's oldest national park.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plitvice_Lakes_National_Park

places.title: Iguazu Falls
places.note:
Hundreds of waterfalls on the border between Argentina and Brazil. Don't miss the Devil's Throat.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iguazu_Falls

places.title: Hạ Long Bay
places.note:
Around 1,600 limestone islands and islets rising from the Gulf of Tonkin. Best seen from a boat.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%E1%BA%A1_Long_Bay

places.title: Moraine Lake
places.note:
Glacier-fed lake in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, bright turquoise in summer.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moraine_Lake

places.title: Zhangjiajie
places.address: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, Hunan, China
places.note:
Thousands of sandstone pillars, said to have inspired the floating mountains in Avatar.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhangjiajie_National_Forest_Park

places.title: Torres del Paine
places.address: Torres del Paine National Park, Chile
places.note:
Three granite towers in Patagonia. The viewpoint at their base is a long day hike.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_del_Paine_National_Park

places.title: Victoria Falls
places.note:
The Zambezi drops over a 1.7 km wide edge between Zambia and Zimbabwe. Locally called Mosi-oa-Tunya, “the smoke that thunders”.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Falls

places.title: Sossusvlei
places.note:
A white salt and clay pan ringed by some of the highest red dunes in the world, in the Namib Desert.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sossusvlei

places.title: Mount Kilimanjaro
places.note:
Africa's highest mountain, 5,895 m: a snow-capped volcano rising alone above the savanna. The pin marks Uhuru Peak, the summit.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kilimanjaro

places.title: Makhtesh Ramon
places.note:
A 40 km long erosion crater in the Negev desert, the largest of its kind in the world.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makhtesh_Ramon

places.title: Lut Desert
places.note:
One of the hottest places on Earth, with long wind-carved ridges called kaluts. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lut_Desert

places.title: Pamukkale
places.note:
White travertine terraces filled with warm spring water, right above the ruins of ancient Hierapolis.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamukkale

places.title: Ilulissat Icefjord
places.note:
Sermeq Kujalleq, one of the fastest-moving glaciers in the world, fills this UNESCO-listed fjord with icebergs. The pin marks the viewpoint near town.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilulissat_Icefjord

places.title: Lofoten
places.note:
Steep peaks straight out of the sea, red fishing cabins and the midnight sun. The photo is the view from Reinebringen above Reine.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lofoten

places.title: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
places.note:
Three limestone peaks in the Dolomites, best seen from the loop trail around them.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tre_Cime_di_Lavaredo

places.title: Cliffs of Moher
places.note:
Sea cliffs rising over 200 m straight out of the Atlantic on Ireland's west coast.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliffs_of_Moher

places.title: Uluru
places.address: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park, Northern Territory, Australia
places.note:
A huge sandstone monolith in the red centre of Australia, sacred to the Aṉangu people. It glows red at sunset.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uluru
